text.p: Following are some of the major events to have occurred on November 23 in history.
1499 - Perkin Warbeck, Flemish imposter and pretender to the throne of King Henry VII of England, was executed in the Tower of London. He claimed to be Richard, Duke of York, son of Edward IV.
1804 - Franklin Pierce, 14th president of the United States, born.
1859 - Willam H. Bonney (Billy the Kid) was born in New York. A notorious outlaw, he shot his first victims when he was only 12. He was eventually killed by Sheriff Pat Garrett.
1876 - Spanish composer Manuel de Falla was born. He was best known for his "Nights in the Gardens of Spain" and his ballet "The Three-Cornered Hat".
1887 - Boris Karloff was born as William Henry Pratt. A stage and screen star, notably in horror films.
1889 - The first jukebox was installed at the Palais Royal Saloon in San Francisco.
1890 - Princess Wilhelmina became Queen of the Netherlands at the age of 10 upon the death of her father William III. Her mother Queen Emma acted as Regent until 1898.
1910 - Dr Hawley Crippen, the first criminal to be caught by radio, was hanged in London for killing his wife.
1961 - The Dominican Republic changed the name of its capital from Ciudad Trujillo to Santo Domingo.
1978 - A cyclone struck the east coast of Sri Lanka, killing at least 1,000 people.
1979 - In Dublin, Thomas McMahon was sentenced to life imprisonment for the assassination of Earl Mountbatten, cousin of Britain's Queen Elisabeth.
1979 - Australian-born film actress Merle Oberon died. In a film career spanning 40 years, she starred notably in "The Private Life of Henry VIII" and "Wuthering Heights".
1980 - An earthquake measuring 7.2 on the Richter scale struck Eboli in southern Italy, killing 2,735 people and injuring at least 7,500.
1983 - The Soviet Union walked out of arms limitation talks in Geneva in protest at the deployment of U.S. Cruise missiles in Europe.
1992 - A neo-Nazi racist attack against Turkish immigrants in Germany left one woman and two children dead. The attack occurred at a guest workers' home in the village of Moelln.
1994 - At least 111 people, mostly women and children, were killed in a stampede after Indian police baton-charged tribal protesters in the western city of Nagpur.
1995 - Serbian President Slobodan Milosevic forced Bosnian Serb hardliners to accept a U.S.-sponsored peace deal, the key to ending 3-1/2 years of U.N. sanctions on rump Yugoslavia.
